Oyster Therapeutics · brandmark brainstorm

The oyster is already a SELFTAC

An oyster is two separate halves, its valves, held together by one reversible joint, the hinge ligament. A SELFTAC is two halves that clasp back together. So none of these adds a pearl or a molecule to a shell: the valves are the two halves, and the hinge, the lip or the seam between them carries the clasp, in the clasp colour. Every shell is drawn with a frilled edge and growth layers, which is what makes an oyster read as an oyster and not a clam, a cowrie or a coffee bean (smooth first sketches read as all three). Each is shown clasped and split: the split state is for motion, the halves coming together in the intro.

01

The ligament

The whole oyster, closed, from above. Its ligament, the joint at the hinge that opens and closes a real oyster, is the clasp, in gold.

The least added: one gold detail, at the one place an oyster actually clasps. It reads as an oyster first at any size.

02

Two valves, one hinge

The oyster opened and laid flat, as on a plate: two valves, near mirror images, joined at the hinge by the gold ligament.

The SELFTAC idea at a glance, two halves held by one clasp, and still unmistakably shellfish.

03

The seam is the linker

The oyster from above, split from hinge to lip. The seam is a zigzag, a chain in a chemist’s skeletal formula, with its middle bond in gold.

A biologist sees an oyster; a chemist sees a linker. The growth layers run across both halves, so it stays one shell.

04

The lip is the linker

A closed oyster from the side, a flat layered lid on a deep cup. The lip where the valves meet is the zigzag chain, with a gold middle bond.

The oyster’s real profile; the zigzag lip is true to life, and chemists read it as a chain.

05

Kintsugi

Kintsugi is the Japanese craft of rejoining broken pieces with gold. The oyster in two halves, the whole seam between them a line of gold.

Halves rejoined, and better for it: a story people already know. The seam keeps the chain’s zigzag, so it is still a linker.

06

Ajar

The side-on oyster of 04 with its lid lifted about the hinge: the zigzag lips part, and the ligament that springs the shell open and shut is gold.

Built to move: in the intro it opens and clasps shut, as a SELFTAC does. Closed, it becomes 04.
